metrics.test_coverage: 15 dedicated tests (new) + 17 Moq-based pre-existing = 32 total PathBasedVideoHasher tests; 262 total across solution

comments.note: AC-3 (duplicate keys): test uses two separate FakeFfprobeRunner instances — one with two streams both having codec_long_name, one with a single stream. Hash equality confirms first-occurrence-wins semantics. Approach is sound.

Malformed JSON from ffprobe is not covered by tests (not in AC scope). Utf8JsonReader would throw JsonException, which would propagate unhandled to the caller. This is acceptable given the spec assumes a well-behaved ffprobe binary; worth noting for a future robustness pass.

15 new tests in VideoIndexer.Tests/PathBasedVideoHasherTests.cs overlap in coverage with 17 existing Moq-based tests in VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests. Both pass. No regression introduced. The Developer's implementation note about eventual test project ownership consolidation is noted.

summary: Code review PASS. Test-only WP. The 15-test suite in PathBasedVideoHasherTests.cs is well-structured, covers all 7 ACs, and uses an independent ComputeExpectedMd5 reimplementation for the known-hash fixture test — correctly avoiding circular dependency on the SUT output. No blocking issues found. No Fix-Forward changes applied.

comments.note: The Theory test for AC-1 uses 5 InlineData cases covering different obfuscated extensions (.raz, .dic, .pkg, .dat, .llz). These cover the majority of the 10 obfuscated extensions. The remaining 5 (.res, .stf, .wwd, .vkg) are omitted but their behaviour is identical — the shortcut path is extension-agnostic once IsObfuscated returns true. Coverage is sufficient.

FakeFfprobeRunner uses OrdinalIgnoreCase for path key comparisons. This is a Windows-first default; on Linux paths are case-sensitive. All test paths are constant strings compared against themselves so there is no practical risk, but a future Linux CI environment could expose subtleties if test paths ever diverge in case.

[documentation-forward] PathBasedVideoHasher.cs documents the non-ASCII metadata collision limitation (ASCII encoding maps any non-ASCII char to '?'). The API documentation for IVideoHasher.ComputeHashAsync should propagate this known limitation to the interface-level docs, so callers relying only on the interface contract are aware of it.

Security attention: ComputeHashAsync has a documented trust boundary note — filePath is not validated against traversal sequences or UNC paths. Review this for threat model fit.
MD5 is used for hashing (spec-mandated). Security auditor should note this is a fingerprinting hash, not a security hash; collision resistance is not required for deduplication purposes.
Non-ASCII metadata collision known limitation is documented in the XML summary of PathBasedVideoHasher.cs.
